description: An isometric hold that builds quad endurance and needs nothing but a wall.
instructions: Stand with your back flat against a wall and walk the feet out about two feet.
Slide down until the thighs are parallel to the floor and the knees are at 90 degrees.
Keep the whole back pressed into the wall and the weight in your heels.
Hold for time, breathing normally rather than holding your breath.

name: Hang Squat
description: Holding straps lets you sit into a deeper squat than you could unassisted -- great for learning depth.
instructions: Grip a pair of suspension straps and lean back with the arms extended.
Set the feet shoulder-width and let the straps take some of your weight.
Sit down into a deep squat, using the straps to stay upright.
Drive back up through the heels, pulling only as much as you need.

name: Hang Lunge
description: An assisted lunge on straps -- the balance support lets you focus purely on the leg drive.
instructions: Hold a strap in each hand and step one foot back into a split stance.
Keep the torso upright with light tension on the straps.
Lower the back knee toward the floor under control.
Drive up through the front heel, using the straps only for balance.

name: Cable Squat Press
description: A squat and overhead press linked on cables, keeping tension on the whole chain.
instructions: Take a handle in each hand from low pulleys and hold them at shoulder height.
Squat down with the chest tall and the cables under tension.
Drive up out of the squat and press both handles overhead as you stand.
Return the handles to your shoulders and squat straight into the next rep.

name: Cable Squat One-Arm Press
description: A single-arm squat-to-press, so the core has to fight rotation on every rep.
instructions: Take one handle from a low pulley and hold it at shoulder height.
Squat down keeping the hips square to the machine.
Drive up and press the handle overhead without twisting the torso.
Lower back to the shoulder and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Cable Forward Lunge
description: A lunge against cable resistance, which keeps the legs loaded even at the top of the rep.
instructions: Take a handle in each hand from low pulleys and step away until the cables are taut.
Stand tall with the handles at your shoulders or sides.
Step forward into a lunge, lowering the back knee toward the floor.
Push back to standing against the cable tension and alternate legs.

name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
description: The best hamstring builder there is: a loaded hinge through a long, controlled stretch.
instructions: Start standing tall with the bar at hip height and a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Unlock the knees slightly and hold that angle -- the knees do not bend further.
Push the hips straight back, letting the bar slide down your thighs.
Stop when the hamstrings reach end range with a flat back, then drive the hips forward to stand.

name: Barbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A near-straight-legged hinge from the floor that loads the hamstrings at maximum length.
instructions: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot and the legs almost straight.
Hinge at the hips to grip the bar, keeping the back flat and the chest up.
Stand up by driving the hips forward, keeping the bar close to your legs.
Lower under control back toward the floor -- stop the set the moment the back rounds.

name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Stiff-Leg Deadlift
description: A one-legged hinge that trains the hamstrings while exposing any balance or hip control issues.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward at the hip, letting the free leg extend straight behind you as a counterweight.
Keep the hips square to the floor rather than letting the free hip open up.
Lower until you feel the hamstring stretch, then drive the hip forward to stand tall.

name: Good Morning
description: A bar-on-back hinge that builds the spinal erectors and hamstrings together. Start very light.
instructions: Rack the bar on your upper traps as you would for a squat and set the feet hip-width.
Unlock the knees slightly and brace the whole midsection hard.
Push the hips back and hinge the torso forward toward parallel with the floor.
Drive the hips forward to return upright, keeping the back flat the entire time.

name: Barbell Glute Bridge
description: Loads the glutes directly at their shortest, strongest position with no lower-back strain.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the bar resting across your hips on a pad.
Set the feet flat, roughly hip-width, close enough that your fingers can brush your heels.
Drive through the heels to push the hips up until the body forms a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes hard at the top, then lower under control without dropping the bar.

name: Hip Thrust
description: The bench-supported glute bridge. Longer range than the floor version and it loads far heavier.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench and the bar across your hips.
Plant the feet flat with the shins vertical at the top of the movement.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips until the torso is parallel to the floor.
Tuck the chin, squeeze the glutes for a beat, and lower under control.

name: Bodyweight Glute Bridge
description: The unloaded starting point for glute training, and a useful warm-up before squats or deadlifts.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat, hip-width apart.
Press the lower back gently into the floor and brace the abs.
Drive through the heels to lift the hips until the body is in a straight line.
Squeeze the glutes at the top for a two-count, then lower slowly.

name: Dumbbell Hamstring Curl
description: A leg curl done with a dumbbell gripped between the feet, for when no machine is available.
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with the legs hanging off the end.
Have a partner place a dumbbell between your feet, or pinch it with your ankles.
Curl the heels toward your glutes by bending at the knees.
Squeeze the hamstrings at the top, then lower under full control.

name: Prone Leg Curl
description: Lying leg curl -- the standard way to train knee flexion, which hinges alone will not do.
instructions: Lie face down with the knees just off the end of the pad and the roller on your lower calves.
Grip the handles and keep the hips pressed into the bench.
Curl the heels toward your glutes as far as the machine allows.
Lower slowly to near-full extension without letting the hips lift.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: Curling with the hips flexed puts the hamstrings on stretch, which many find more effective than prone.
instructions: Set the seat and thigh pad so your knees line up with the machine pivot.
Sit back with the roller resting on your lower calves and the thigh pad locked down.
Curl the legs down and back as far as they will travel.
Return slowly to a full stretch, keeping the back against the pad.

name: Single-Leg Curl
description: One hamstring at a time, useful after an injury or for evening out a strength difference.
instructions: Set the machine as normal but place only one leg under the roller.
Keep the hips square and pressed into the pad.
Curl the heel toward your glute through the full range.
Lower slowly to extension, then complete the set and switch legs.

name: Standing Leg Curl
description: A single-leg standing curl, which also makes the standing leg work to stabilise you.
instructions: Stand in the machine with the roller behind one ankle and hold the support pads.
Keep the torso upright and the hips square throughout.
Curl the heel up toward your glute without letting the hip swing back.
Lower under control and finish the set before switching legs.

name: Exercise Ball Single-Leg Curl
description: A bodyweight hamstring curl on a ball, which trains both knee flexion and hip extension at once.
instructions: Lie on your back with one heel on top of an exercise ball and the other leg raised.
Drive the hips up so your body forms a straight line from shoulders to heel.
Curl the ball in toward your glutes by bending the working knee.
Roll it back out under control without letting the hips drop.

name: Glute Machine
description: A standing hip extension machine that isolates the glutes with no lower-back involvement.
instructions: Set the pad against the back of one thigh and hold the chest support.
Stand tall on the supporting leg with the hips square.
Drive the working leg back by extending the hip, not by arching the lower back.
Squeeze the glute at the top, then return under control.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
description: Trains the glute medius, which stabilises the hip and keeps the knees tracking properly under load.
instructions: Sit with the pads against the outside of your thighs and knees together.
Sit up tall with the back flat against the pad.
Push the knees apart against the resistance as far as they will travel.
Return slowly under tension rather than letting the pads snap back.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
description: A standing cable abduction, which trains the same muscles as the machine but with a balance demand.
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low pulley and fasten it to the ankle furthest from the machine.
Stand side-on, holding the frame for balance with the hips square.
Sweep the working leg out to the side without leaning the torso away.
Return slowly against the cable, then finish the set and switch sides.

name: Hip Adduction Machine
description: Direct inner-thigh work, which most squat and lunge patterns under-train.
instructions: Sit with the pads on the inside of your thighs and the legs spread apart.
Sit tall with the back flat against the pad and grip the handles.
Squeeze the knees together against the resistance.
Return slowly out to a stretch, staying in control at the end range.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
description: A standing adduction on cables, adding a stability demand on the supporting leg.
instructions: Cuff the ankle nearest the machine to a low pulley and step out until the cable is taut.
Stand side-on, holding the frame with the hips square and torso upright.
Pull the working leg across your body against the resistance.
Let it return slowly out to the side, then swap sides.

name: Standing Rear Kick
description: A bodyweight hip extension you can do anywhere, good as a warm-up or a finisher.
instructions: Stand tall, holding a wall or chair for balance, with the core braced.
Drive one leg straight back by extending at the hip.
Squeeze the glute at the top without arching the lower back to get more range.
Return under control and repeat, then switch legs.

name: Standing Side Kick
description: Bodyweight abduction that trains the side of the hip -- useful for knee tracking and hip stability.
instructions: Stand tall with the hands on your hips or holding a support.
Brace the core so the torso stays vertical.
Lift one leg straight out to the side as high as you can without leaning.
Lower slowly under control and repeat, then switch legs.

name: Leg Stabilizer
description: A single-leg balance and hip-control drill that shores up the stabilisers around the knee and hip.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a soft bend in the knee and the core braced.
Hold the hips level -- do not let the free-side hip drop.
Move the free leg slowly through a controlled range while staying balanced.
Hold for time on each side, keeping the standing knee tracking over the foot.

name: Bent-Over Row Stabilizer
description: A hinge-and-hold drill that teaches you to keep a flat back before you load rows and deadlifts.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width and a soft bend in the knees.
Hinge at the hips until the torso is close to parallel with the floor.
Hold that position with the back flat, chest up and the core braced.
Return to standing by driving the hips forward, keeping the spine neutral throughout.

name: Standing Barbell Calf Raise
description: A straight-leg calf raise, which is what loads the gastrocnemius -- the muscle that gives calves shape.
instructions: Rack a bar on your upper back and stand with the balls of your feet on a raised block.
Let the heels drop below the block until you feel a deep stretch.
Press up onto the toes as high as you can go and pause at the top.
Lower slowly back into the stretch -- never bounce out of the bottom.

name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
description: The standard machine calf raise, easy to load heavily and easy to take to failure.
instructions: Set the shoulder pads so you are slightly bent at the knees when the heels drop.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform with the heels hanging off.
Lower the heels until you feel a full stretch through the calf.
Press up onto the toes and squeeze hard at the top for a beat.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
description: One calf at a time using just bodyweight, which is enough load for most people to start with.
instructions: Stand on one foot with the ball of that foot on a step, holding a wall for balance.
Let the heel drop below the step until you feel a strong stretch.
Press up onto the toes as high as you can go.
Pause at the top, lower slowly, and finish the set before switching legs.

name: Rotary Calf Machine
description: A seated rotary calf machine that keeps constant tension through the full range of the raise.
instructions: Set the seat and pad so the balls of your feet rest on the platform with the knees under the pad.
Let the heels drop into a stretched position.
Press through the toes to raise the pad as high as it will travel.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly back into the stretch.

name: Donkey Calf Press
description: Calf raises on the leg press with a narrow, straight-ahead stance -- the default variation.
instructions: Sit in the leg press and place the balls of your feet at the bottom of the platform, hip-width apart.
Release the safeties and straighten the legs without locking the knees.
Let the toes push the platform away by pressing through the balls of your feet.
Lower slowly until you feel a full calf stretch, then press again.

name: Wide-Stance Donkey Calf Press
description: A wider foot placement on the leg press, which shifts emphasis toward the inner head of the calf.
instructions: Place the balls of your feet on the platform noticeably wider than hip-width.
Keep the toes pointing straight ahead and the legs almost straight.
Press the platform away through the balls of the feet as far as it will go.
Lower slowly into a deep stretch before the next rep.

name: Toes-Out Donkey Calf Press
description: Turning the toes out biases the inner head of the gastrocnemius.
instructions: Set the balls of your feet on the platform with the toes angled outward.
Straighten the legs without locking the knees and release the safeties.
Press through the balls of the feet to full extension of the ankle.
Lower under control into the stretch, keeping the toe angle consistent.

name: Toes-In Donkey Calf Press
description: Turning the toes in shifts the work toward the outer head, which builds width from behind.
instructions: Place the balls of your feet on the platform with the toes angled inward.
Extend the legs and release the safety catches.
Press the platform away by extending through the ankles.
Lower slowly to a full stretch, keeping the knees soft throughout.

name: Plank
description: An anti-extension hold that teaches the core its real job: resisting movement, not creating it.
instructions: Set the elbows directly under the shoulders with the forearms flat and feet hip-width.
Tuck the pelvis under and squeeze the glutes so the lower back flattens out.
Hold a straight line from heels to head with the abs braced hard.
Stop the set when the hips start to sag -- quality beats duration here.

name: Plank On Exercise Ball
description: A plank with the forearms on a ball, so the core has to fight constant micro-movement.
instructions: Place your forearms on top of an exercise ball with the elbows under your shoulders.
Walk the feet back until the body forms a straight line.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes to keep the ball completely still.
Hold for time, stopping as soon as the hips drop or the ball starts to drift.

name: Sit-Up
description: The classic full-range ab exercise. Done properly it is far more than just a crunch.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor.
Cross the arms over your chest rather than pulling on your neck.
Curl the spine up one vertebra at a time until your torso is upright.
Lower back down with the same control, keeping tension on the abs throughout.

name: Decline Sit-Up
description: Adding a decline lengthens the range of motion and makes bodyweight sit-ups genuinely hard.
instructions: Hook your feet under the pads on a decline bench with the knees bent.
Cross the arms over your chest and start lying back on the bench.
Curl up until your torso is close to vertical, leading with the sternum.
Lower slowly back to the start without letting your back slam down.

name: Janda Sit-Up
description: A sit-up variation that switches off the hip flexors so the abs do all the work.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and have a partner hold your calves, or press your heels into a wall.
Actively pull the heels toward your glutes for the whole set -- this shuts off the hip flexors.
Curl up slowly, keeping the tension on the hamstrings the whole way.
Lower under control. Expect far fewer reps than a normal sit-up.

name: Floor Crunch
description: A short-range crunch focused on the upper abs, and the simplest ab exercise to learn.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent, feet flat and hands lightly beside your head.
Press the lower back into the floor before you move.
Curl the shoulder blades a few inches off the floor by shortening the abs.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly without resting between reps.

name: Deep Crunch
description: A crunch taken through a longer range than the floor version for a much stronger contraction.
instructions: Lie back with the knees bent and the arms extended overhead or across the chest.
Begin by pressing the lower back down and tilting the pelvis.
Curl up as high as you can, driving the ribcage toward the pelvis.
Lower slowly all the way back, keeping the abs loaded at the bottom.

name: Psycho Crunch
description: A high-intensity crunch variation that keeps the abs under tension for the entire set.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs raised and the knees bent to 90 degrees.
Curl the shoulders up off the floor and hold that position throughout.
Crunch the ribcage and pelvis toward each other in short, hard pulses.
Do not let the shoulders or feet touch down until the set is finished.

name: Elbow To Knee Crunch
description: A rotational crunch that brings the obliques in alongside the front abs.
instructions: Lie on your back with the hands lightly beside your head and the knees bent.
Curl up and rotate, driving one elbow toward the opposite knee.
Squeeze the oblique at the top rather than yanking on your neck.
Lower under control and alternate sides on every rep.

name: Standing Elbow To Knee Crunch
description: A standing version of the cross-body crunch that also gets the heart rate up.
instructions: Stand tall with the hands behind your head and the elbows out wide.
Drive one knee up and across while crunching the opposite elbow down to meet it.
Squeeze the oblique at the point of contact.
Return to standing and alternate sides continuously.

name: Side Oblique Crunch
description: A lateral-flexion crunch that trains the obliques through side bending.
instructions: Lie on your side with the knees bent and stacked, bottom arm across your body.
Place the top hand lightly behind your head.
Crunch sideways, lifting the shoulder toward your hip.
Lower slowly and complete the set before switching sides.

name: Advanced Side Oblique Crunch
description: A harder oblique crunch with the legs extended, so the whole side of the trunk works.
instructions: Lie on your side with the legs straight and stacked, top hand behind your head.
Raise the legs and the torso toward each other at the same time.
Squeeze the obliques hard at the top of the crunch.
Lower both ends slowly under control, then switch sides.

name: Oblique Floor Crunch
description: A crunch with the legs dropped to one side, isolating one oblique at a time.
instructions: Lie on your back and let both bent knees fall to one side.
Keep the shoulders flat and place the hands lightly beside your head.
Crunch straight up while the legs stay rotated to the side.
Lower slowly, finish the set, then drop the legs to the other side.

name: Leg Lift
description: The staple lower-ab exercise -- most of the work happens in the last few inches at the bottom.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes and the legs straight.
Press the lower back into the floor and keep it there for the whole set.
Raise both legs until they are vertical, keeping them straight.
Lower slowly, stopping just before the heels touch or the lower back lifts.

name: Maximum Leg Lift
description: A leg lift taken past vertical into a hip raise, hitting the lower abs far harder.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes or gripping a support behind your head.
Raise the straight legs up to vertical.
Keep going and lift the hips off the floor, driving the feet toward the ceiling.
Lower the hips then the legs, under control, all the way back down.

name: Isolation Leg Lift
description: A leg lift with a shortened range that keeps constant tension on the lower abs.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your lower back for support.
Raise the legs to about 45 degrees and hold that as your bottom position.
Lift the legs to vertical, then lower only back to 45 degrees.
Never let the legs rest on the floor between reps.

name: Isolation Leg Lift Hip Thrust
description: Adds a vertical hip drive to the leg lift, which is where the lower abs really engage.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes and the legs raised to vertical.
Press the feet straight up toward the ceiling by lifting the hips off the floor.
Keep the movement small and controlled -- do not swing the legs to generate it.
Lower the hips back down without letting the legs drop out of position.

name: Hip Thrust Crunch
description: A combined reverse crunch and hip thrust that trains the lower abs from both directions.
instructions: Lie flat with the legs raised straight up and the arms out for support.
Curl the pelvis toward your ribs to bring the hips off the floor.
Press the feet toward the ceiling at the top of the movement.
Lower with control back to the start, keeping the legs vertical.

name: Hip Thrust Crunch With Oblique Twist
description: The hip thrust crunch with a rotation added at the top, bringing the obliques in hard.
instructions: Start lying flat with the legs raised straight up toward the ceiling.
Drive the hips up as in a normal hip thrust crunch.
At the top, twist the hips slightly to one side before lowering.
Alternate the twist direction on each rep, keeping the movement controlled.

name: Flutter Kicks
description: A continuous-tension lower-ab drill where the legs never touch down.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes and the legs raised a few inches off the floor.
Press the lower back firmly into the floor.
Kick the legs up and down in small, quick alternating movements.
Keep the legs straight and off the ground for the whole set.

name: Scissor Flutter Kicks
description: Flutter kicks crossed side to side, which brings the inner thighs and deep core into play.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes and both legs raised slightly off the floor.
Keep the lower back pressed down throughout.
Cross one straight leg over the other, then switch, scissoring continuously.
Keep the movement small and never let the heels touch the floor.

name: Alternating Abdominal Kick
description: A single-leg lower-ab drill, easier on the lower back than lifting both legs at once.
instructions: Lie flat with the hands under your glutes and both legs raised.
Lower one straight leg toward the floor while the other stays up.
Stop just before the heel touches and reverse the movement.
Alternate legs, keeping the lower back pinned down the whole time.

name: Alternating Reverse Crunch To Toe Touch
description: A combination rep that pairs a reverse crunch with a cross-body toe touch.
instructions: Lie flat with the legs raised straight toward the ceiling.
Perform a reverse crunch, curling the hips off the floor.
As you lower, crunch up and reach one hand across to the opposite toe.
Alternate the reaching hand on each rep and keep the legs from dropping.

name: V-Up
description: Upper and lower abs contract at once as the body folds into a V. Deceptively hard.
instructions: Lie flat with the arms extended overhead and the legs straight.
In one movement, lift the torso and the legs to meet over your hips.
Reach the hands toward the toes at the top of the rep.
Lower both ends back down under control without touching the floor.

name: Toe Touch
description: A short-range upper-ab crunch performed with the legs held vertical.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs pointing straight up at the ceiling.
Reach both hands toward your toes.
Crunch the shoulder blades off the floor and squeeze the abs at the top.
Lower slowly and keep the legs vertical the whole set.

name: Alternating Toe Touch
description: A cross-body toe touch that adds rotation to bring in the obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs raised straight up.
Crunch up and reach one hand across toward the opposite foot.
Squeeze the oblique at the top of the reach.
Lower under control and alternate hands on each rep.

name: Hanging Leg Raise
description: The straight-leg progression of the hanging knee raise, and one of the hardest ab exercises there is.
instructions: Hang from a bar with an overhand grip and the legs straight below you.
Tilt the pelvis back to switch the abs on before the legs move.
Raise the straight legs until they are level with the bar, or as high as you can control.
Lower slowly without swinging -- if you swing, go back to knee raises.

name: Toes To Bar
description: A full-range hanging raise where the feet touch the bar. Demands core strength and hamstring flexibility.
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders.
Pull down slightly on the bar with the lats to create tension.
Curl the pelvis and drive the straight legs all the way up to touch the bar.
Lower under control back to the hang without swinging into the next rep.

name: Hanging Cross-Body Knee Raise
description: A hanging knee raise driven diagonally, which loads the obliques far more than the straight version.
instructions: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip and the body still.
Raise the knees up and across toward one shoulder.
Squeeze the oblique at the top rather than just swinging the legs over.
Lower under control and alternate sides on each rep.

name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
description: One of the hardest oblique exercises there is -- rotating the legs while hanging from the bar.
instructions: Hang from the bar and raise the straight legs up until they are near vertical.
Keep the shoulders tight and pulled down away from the ears.
Rotate the legs to one side like a windscreen wiper, controlling the descent.
Bring them back through centre and over to the other side.

name: Hanging Serratus Crunch
description: A hanging crunch that targets the serratus and deep core through scapular depression.
instructions: Hang from the bar with the arms straight and the shoulders relaxed up by your ears.
Without bending the arms, pull the shoulders down and the ribcage up.
At the same time curl the pelvis toward the ribs.
Return to the relaxed hang and repeat with control.

name: Dip Bar Leg Raise
description: A dip combined with a leg raise, which keeps the abs loaded while the arms hold you up.
instructions: Support yourself on parallel bars with the arms locked out.
Perform a dip, lowering until the upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Press back to lockout, then raise the legs up in front of you.
Lower the legs under control and go straight into the next dip.

name: Suspended Leg Raise
description: A leg raise from a captain's chair or dip bars, with the back supported so there is less swing.
instructions: Support yourself on your forearms with the back against the pad and legs hanging.
Press the lower back into the pad and tilt the pelvis before you lift.
Raise the knees or straight legs up toward your chest.
Lower under control without arching the back off the support.

name: Dumbbell Hanging Knee Raise
description: A weighted hanging knee raise for when bodyweight sets stop being challenging.
instructions: Pinch a light dumbbell between your feet and hang from the bar.
Settle the body so there is no swing before the first rep.
Raise the knees toward your chest, curling the pelvis at the top.
Lower slowly and keep the dumbbell locked between your feet throughout.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
description: The most demanding anti-extension exercise you can do, and it hits the whole core at once.
instructions: Kneel on a mat holding a loaded barbell with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Tuck the pelvis under and brace the abs hard before you move.
Roll the bar forward as far as you can while keeping the lower back flat.
Pull the bar back in using the abs -- stop shortening the range the moment the back arches.

name: Ball Crunch
description: The ball lets the spine extend below horizontal, giving the abs a far longer range than a floor crunch.
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball and walk out until your lower back is supported on top of it.
Let the torso extend back over the ball until you feel the abs stretch.
Crunch up by curling the ribcage toward your pelvis.
Lower back over the ball slowly, keeping the hips level.

name: Weighted Ball Crunch
description: A ball crunch with a plate held on the chest -- the simplest way to progress ab training.
instructions: Set up on the ball as for a normal ball crunch, holding a plate across your chest.
Extend back over the ball until you feel the stretch.
Crunch up, keeping the plate pinned to your chest rather than swinging it.
Lower slowly under control back to the stretched position.

name: Advanced Oblique Ball Crunch
description: A ball crunch with rotation, which loads the obliques through their full stretched range.
instructions: Position yourself on the ball so it supports the side of your lower back.
Let the torso extend over the ball to stretch the obliques.
Crunch up and rotate, bringing the shoulder toward the opposite hip.
Lower slowly, then complete the set before switching sides.

name: Ball Pass
description: Passing a ball between hands and feet, which links the upper and lower abs in one rep.
instructions: Lie flat with the arms extended overhead holding an exercise ball.
Bring the ball and your legs up to meet over your hips.
Pass the ball to your feet and pinch it between the ankles.
Lower both ends to the floor without touching, then pass it back to your hands.

name: Medicine Ball Floor Crunch
description: A weighted floor crunch using a medicine ball held overhead or on the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and hold a medicine ball at your chest.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace.
Crunch the shoulder blades off the floor, keeping the ball close to your body.
Lower slowly without letting the head rest between reps.

name: Cable Ab Pulldown
description: A kneeling cable crunch -- the easiest way to add real progressive load to your ab training.
instructions: Attach a rope to a high pulley, kneel facing the machine and hold the rope beside your head.
Hinge slightly at the hips so the cable is under tension, then lock the hips in place.
Crunch down by rounding the spine and driving the elbows toward your thighs.
Return up slowly, keeping the hips still so the abs do the work, not the hip flexors.

name: Abdominal Crunch Machine
description: A plate-loaded crunch machine, which makes progressive overload on the abs straightforward.
instructions: Set the seat so the pads sit comfortably against your chest and shoulders.
Grip the handles and hook your feet under the pads if the machine has them.
Crunch forward by rounding the spine rather than folding at the hips.
Return slowly under control without letting the weight stack rest.

name: Oblique Crunch Machine
description: A machine that loads trunk rotation, which is hard to overload any other way.
instructions: Set the seat and lock your legs into the machine so the hips cannot move.
Grip the handles with the torso upright.
Rotate the torso to one side against the resistance, squeezing the oblique.
Return slowly to centre, then complete the set and switch sides.

name: Cable Wood Chopper
description: A diagonal rotational pull that trains the obliques the way they actually work in sport.
instructions: Set a pulley high and grip the handle with both hands, standing side-on to the machine.
Start with the arms extended up and across toward the pulley.
Pull down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating through the trunk.
Let the cable draw you back up under control and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Cable Torso Twist
description: A horizontal rotation against cable resistance, keeping the obliques loaded through the whole arc.
instructions: Set the pulley at chest height and grip the handle with both hands, standing side-on.
Step out until the cable is taut with the arms extended in front of you.
Rotate the torso away from the machine, keeping the arms straight and hips fairly still.
Return under control, resisting the pull all the way back.

name: Landmine Oblique Twist
description: A loaded rotation with a barbell that builds real rotational strength through the trunk.
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell and hold the other end with both hands at chest height.
Stand with the feet shoulder-width and the arms extended.
Rotate the bar down and across to one hip, pivoting the back foot as you turn.
Bring it back up through centre and over to the other side under control.

name: Standing Oblique Crunch With Weight
description: A standing side bend under load, which trains the obliques in lateral flexion.
instructions: Stand tall holding a dumbbell or plate in one hand at your side.
Keep the shoulders square and the hips still.
Bend sideways toward the loaded side, letting the weight travel down your leg.
Pull yourself back upright using the opposite oblique, then switch sides.

name: Standing Barbell Torso Twist
description: A light rotational drill with a bar across the shoulders, useful as a warm-up before heavy lifting.
instructions: Rest an empty or light bar across your upper back and grip it wide.
Stand with the feet shoulder-width and the knees soft.
Rotate the torso smoothly to one side, keeping the hips facing forward.
Rotate through to the other side, staying controlled rather than swinging.

name: Standing Dumbbell Torso Twist
description: A rotation drill holding dumbbells out in front, which lengthens the lever on the obliques.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand out in front of your chest with the elbows bent.
Stand tall with the core braced and the knees soft.
Rotate the torso to one side while keeping the hips square.
Return through centre and rotate to the other side under control.

name: Seated Alternating Oblique Twist
description: The classic seated Russian twist -- simple, portable and effective for the obliques.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the knees bent and lean back to about 45 degrees.
Lift the feet off the floor if you want a harder version.
Rotate the torso to touch the floor beside one hip.
Rotate through to the other side, keeping the chest up and the back flat.

name: Weighted Floor Oblique Twist
description: A loaded Russian twist, which is how you actually progress rotational core work.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the knees bent, holding a plate or medicine ball at your chest.
Lean back to around 45 degrees and lift the feet if you can hold the position.
Rotate the weight to one side and tap it beside your hip.
Rotate through to the other side without rounding the lower back.

name: Floor Wiper
description: A lying windscreen-wiper rotation that trains the obliques through a long, controlled arc.
instructions: Lie flat with the arms out to the sides for support and the legs raised to vertical.
Keep both shoulders pressed into the floor throughout.
Lower the straight legs to one side as far as you can control.
Bring them back to vertical using the obliques, then go to the other side.

name: Stomach Vacuum
description: Trains the transverse abdominis, the deep muscle that pulls the waist in. No load required.
instructions: Stand, kneel or lie down and exhale all the air out of your lungs.
Pull your belly button back toward your spine as hard as you can.
Hold the vacuum for 15 to 20 seconds while breathing shallowly.
Release, take a few normal breaths, and repeat for several rounds.

name: Twist-Ups
description: A sit-up with a rotation at the top, so the obliques finish what the abs start.
instructions: Lie back with the knees bent and the hands lightly beside your head.
Curl the torso up as you would for a sit-up.
At the top, rotate the shoulders to one side and squeeze the oblique.
Lower back down under control and alternate the rotation each rep.

name: Medicine Ball Mountain Climbers
description: Mountain climbers with the hands on a ball, which adds a heavy stability demand on top of the core work.
instructions: Set both hands on a medicine ball and hold a rigid plank position.
Brace the abs so the hips stay level with the shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly.
Keep the ball completely still and the hips from bouncing up and down.

name: Burpee
description: The classic full-body conditioning movement -- a squat, a push-up and a jump in one rep.
instructions: Start standing, then squat down and place your hands on the floor in front of you.
Kick the feet back into a plank and perform a push-up.
Jump the feet back under your hips into a low squat.
Explode straight up into a jump, then land softly into the next rep.

name: Burp N Jack
description: A burpee with a jumping jack built in, which keeps the heart rate high for longer.
instructions: Drop into a squat, plant your hands and kick back into a plank.
Perform a jumping jack with your feet while holding the plank.
Jump the feet back under your hips.
Explode up into a jump and land softly straight into the next rep.

name: Burpee Sit-Thru
description: A burpee with a rotational sit-through added, which brings the obliques and hips into it.
instructions: Perform a standard burpee down into the plank position.
From the plank, pull one knee under your body and rotate the hips through to face upward.
Reverse back into the plank and repeat on the other side.
Jump the feet in and stand up to complete the rep.

name: Box Jump
description: A vertical jump onto a raised platform that trains explosive power in the legs.
instructions: Stand about a foot back from the box with the feet hip-width apart.
Dip into a quarter squat and swing the arms back.
Drive up and forward, landing softly on the box with the knees bent and the feet flat.
Stand up fully on the box, then step down -- do not jump down.

name: Squat Jump
description: A squat finished with a maximal jump, training the legs to produce force quickly.
instructions: Stand with the feet shoulder-width and drop into a squat.
Explode up out of the bottom and jump as high as you can.
Land on the balls of your feet and absorb the impact by bending the knees.
Sink straight back into the squat and repeat without pausing.

name: Sprint
description: Maximal-effort running. The most effective conditioning tool there is, and the easiest to injure yourself with.
instructions: Warm up thoroughly -- at least ten minutes of easy work and dynamic drills.
Start with a forward lean and drive the first few steps hard from the ground.
Run tall with the elbows at 90 degrees and the arms driving straight forward and back.
Take full recovery between efforts so each sprint is close to maximum speed.

name: Lateral Shuffle
description: Side-to-side movement that trains the hips in a plane most gym work completely ignores.
instructions: Get into an athletic stance with the knees bent and the chest up.
Push off the trailing foot to move sideways without crossing your feet.
Stay low the whole time -- do not bob up and down between steps.
Shuffle for a set distance, then change direction and repeat.

name: Lateral Cone Drill
description: A high-knee agility drill over cones that builds foot speed and coordination.
instructions: Set a line of cones or markers about a foot apart.
Stand side-on at one end in an athletic stance.
Drive the knees high and step laterally over each cone as fast as you can.
Work back in the other direction and keep the feet quick and light throughout.

name: Lateral Bench Hop
description: Explosive side-to-side hops over a bench, training lateral power and landing control.
instructions: Stand beside a bench with the feet together and the knees softly bent.
Hop sideways over the bench, keeping the feet together.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with the knees bent to absorb the impact.
Immediately hop back over -- start with a low object and build up.

name: Bear Crawl
description: A crawling pattern that lights up the core and shoulders while getting the heart rate up fast.
instructions: Start on your hands and knees, then lift the knees an inch off the floor.
Keep the hips low and level with the shoulders.
Crawl forward by moving the opposite hand and foot together.
Keep the hips from swaying side to side -- move slower if they do.

name: Dumbbell Bear Crawl
description: A bear crawl gripping dumbbells, which adds a heavy grip and shoulder-stability demand.
instructions: Grip a hex dumbbell in each hand and get into the bear crawl position with the knees just off the floor.
Keep the wrists locked straight over the dumbbells and the hips low.
Crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together.
Keep the dumbbells from tipping and stop the set once the hips start swaying.

name: Groiner
description: A total-body exhaustion drill that hits the lower abs, hip flexors, shoulders and quads at once.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with the core braced hard.
Jump both feet forward so they land outside your hands.
Jump them straight back into the plank position.
Repeat continuously, keeping the hips from piking up between reps.

name: Shin Slaps
description: A high-knee running drill where the hands slap the shins, driving knee height and cadence.
instructions: Stand tall with the hands held at about hip height in front of you.
Run on the spot, driving the knees up to meet your hands.
Slap the shins at the top of each knee drive.
Stay on the balls of your feet and keep the cadence fast.

name: Medicine Ball Chest Throw
description: An explosive pressing throw that trains the chest to produce force fast, not just slowly.
instructions: Lie on a bench or the floor with a partner standing over you holding a medicine ball.
Catch the ball at your chest and absorb it by bending the elbows.
Immediately reverse and throw the ball straight back up as hard as you can.
Reset your position and repeat -- use a light ball and keep the reps sharp.

name: Medicine Ball Throw-Up
description: A sit-up finished with an overhead throw, linking core flexion to an explosive upper-body drive.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent, holding a medicine ball at your chest.
Sit up explosively, keeping the ball close to your body.
At the top, throw the ball up to a partner or a wall.
Catch it, lower under control, and go straight into the next rep.

name: Cannonballs
description: A tuck-and-extend core drill performed continuously, so the abs never get a break.
instructions: Sit on the floor leaning back with the hands on the ground behind you for support.
Extend the legs out straight without letting the heels touch the floor.
Pull the knees back in toward your chest, curling the pelvis as you do.
Repeat continuously, keeping the chest up and the lower back from rounding hard.

name: Hover Glide
description: A dynamic plank variation that slides the body forward and back under constant core tension.
instructions: Set up in a forearm plank with the elbows under the shoulders.
Brace the abs and squeeze the glutes to lock the body straight.
Rock the body forward so the shoulders travel past the elbows.
Rock back to the start, keeping the hips level and the core tight throughout.

name: Fusion Glide
description: A moving plank that combines a glide with a rotation, hitting the whole core in one drill.
instructions: Start in a forearm plank with the body locked straight.
Glide forward until the shoulders pass the elbows.
Rotate slightly to one side as you return, engaging the obliques.
Alternate the rotation direction each rep and keep the hips from dropping.

name: Toe-Driver
description: A plank-based drive that alternates driving the toes toward the hands, hitting the lower abs hard.
instructions: Start in a push-up plank with the core braced and the hips level.
Drive one foot forward toward the outside of the same-side hand.
Return it to the plank under control without letting the hips rise.
Alternate sides, keeping the upper body completely still.

name: Advanced Toe-Driver
description: A harder toe-driver with a cross-body drive that pulls the obliques into every rep.
instructions: Hold a strict push-up plank with the shoulders stacked over the wrists.
Drive one knee forward and across toward the opposite elbow.
Squeeze the oblique at the top rather than just moving the leg.
Return to the plank under control and alternate sides.

name: Triple-Threat
description: A three-movement dumbbell complex done back to back, which is as much conditioning as it is strength.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and start with the feet shoulder-width apart.
Perform the first movement of the complex for the prescribed reps without putting the weights down.
Flow straight into the second and then the third movement with no rest between them.
Rest only after all three are complete, then repeat the whole sequence.

name: Star Spangled Switch
description: A jumping switch drill that trains coordination and conditioning at the same time.
instructions: Start in a split stance with the arms out to the sides.
Jump and switch the legs in the air, landing in the opposite stance.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with the knees bent.
Keep the switches continuous and the torso upright throughout.

name: Duck And Dodge
description: A lateral ducking drill borrowed from boxing footwork -- great for hips, knees and conditioning.
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance with the knees bent and the hands up.
Dip and shift your weight to one side, ducking under an imaginary punch.
Come up on the other side and immediately dip back the other way.
Keep the movement continuous and stay low between reps.

name: Cable Bow And Arrow
description: A single-arm cable pull with a rotation, training the upper back and trunk together.
instructions: Set a pulley at chest height and take the handle in the far hand, standing side-on.
Extend the arm out toward the machine and set an athletic stance.
Pull the handle back to your ribs while rotating the torso away from the machine.
Return under control and complete the set before switching sides.

name: Cable Canoe Row
description: An alternating rotational row that mimics a paddling stroke, tying the back and core together.
instructions: Take a handle from a mid-height pulley with both hands, standing side-on in a staggered stance.
Reach forward and across your body toward the machine.
Pull back and past your hip in a paddling arc, rotating through the trunk.
Return under control and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Cable Golf Swing
description: A rotational sweep against cable resistance that trains the trunk through a sports-specific arc.
instructions: Set a low pulley and grip the handle with both hands, standing side-on.
Set up in a hinged athletic stance as if addressing a ball.
Sweep the handle up and across your body, rotating the hips and trunk together.
Control the return along the same path and repeat, then switch sides.

name: Cable Lunge Chest Press
description: A standing cable press from a lunge stance, pairing an upper-body push with a lower-body hold.
instructions: Take a handle in each hand from chest-height pulleys, facing away from the machine.
Step forward into a lunge and hold that position.
Press both handles forward until the arms are extended.
Return to the chest under control without letting the torso rotate.

name: Cable Static Lunge Row
description: A low row performed while holding a static lunge, so the legs and back work at the same time.
instructions: Take handles from a low pulley and step back into a lunge position.
Hold the lunge with the back knee just off the floor and the torso upright.
Row both handles to your ribs, driving the elbows back.
Extend the arms forward under control without standing up out of the lunge.

name: Cable Static Squat Row
description: A cable row held in a static squat -- upper-back work with a serious leg endurance component.
instructions: Take handles from a low pulley and sink into a half squat.
Hold that squat depth for the whole set with the chest tall.
Row the handles to your sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Extend the arms back out slowly without rising out of the squat.
